Periodontal therapy / Scaling & Root Planing

When gum health needs more than a routine cleaning

Bleeding, tenderness, changes around the gums, or a recommendation for a deeper cleaning deserve a clear explanation. The consultation determines what the concern means and which care path is appropriate.

Scaling and root planing, often called SRP or a deep cleaning, is the confirmed periodontal service in this phase. It addresses deposits below the gumline and may be followed by a maintenance plan when the clinician recommends it.

Confirmed care paths

  • Scaling & Root Planing (SRP)
  • Periodontal evaluation and maintenance planning
  • Routine preventive care when a deeper periodontal service is not indicated
  • Referral when the clinical scope requires it
Practice context

Scaling & Root Planing is restored as a visible, directly linked service in the Phase 3 catalog instead of being hidden inside a modal.

01

Who may be a candidate

People with gum-health concerns or a recommendation for scaling and root planing may request a periodontal evaluation.

02

What an online page cannot decide

Symptoms alone do not determine the correct treatment. The clinician evaluates the gums and supporting structures; SRP is not automatically appropriate for every patient.

Start with clarity

Your Winter Park consultation

  1. 01

    Discuss bleeding, sensitivity, tenderness, or the concern that led you to call.

  2. 02

    Complete the periodontal evaluation and any diagnostic steps the clinician considers relevant.

  3. 03

    Review whether SRP, routine care, maintenance, referral, or another option fits the findings.

Before you decide

What to expect

If SRP is recommended, the practice explains the areas involved, the appointments, comfort plan, aftercare, and maintenance. This page does not promise a fixed number of visits or a particular result.

Ask about local comfort measures, sensitivity, and how the visit will be paced. If dental anxiety is part of the concern, review the Sedation Dentistry page and discuss what is clinically appropriate with the team.

Possible benefits

  • A specific path for gum-health concerns that need evaluation
  • Clearer distinction between routine cleaning and periodontal therapy
  • Maintenance planning that can be revisited with the practice

Limitations & alternatives

  • SRP is not a universal treatment and requires evaluation
  • Care may involve more than one visit or ongoing maintenance
  • Referral or a different level of care may be appropriate

After your visit

Care, recovery & maintenance

Use the SRP section of the care hub as a supplement to the practice's instructions. Keep recommended maintenance visits and call the office if discomfort, bleeding, or another concern changes.

Questions patients ask

Start with the questions that matter to you

What is scaling and root planing?

It is a periodontal cleaning approach that addresses deposits below the gumline. The clinician determines whether SRP is appropriate after evaluating the gums.

Is SRP the same as a routine cleaning?

No. The two services serve different purposes, and the practice determines which type of care fits the evaluation.

Will there be a maintenance plan after SRP?

The practice may recommend follow-up or periodontal maintenance based on the individual findings. The interval and scope are not universal.

Can I ask about sensitivity or anxiety?

Yes. Tell the team when you request the evaluation so comfort questions can be included in planning.
